title: Selecting a result records a usage analytics event
comment:
Failed on staging (app.staging.shopview.com), workplace Staging Heavy Duty - 9919, build v26.39.1-02c6b6c, 28 September 2026.

Nothing is recorded when somebody picks a search result.

A search was run, a result was clicked, and every request the page made was watched. The only thing that looks like a record is a Google Analytics message - and it carries the event name "page_view" and does not mention search anywhere. The same message fires when you simply walk to the Parts page without searching at all, so it is an ordinary page view, not a record of the search selection. Nothing is sent to ShopView's own system about the choice that was made.

So there is no way to learn what people search for, what they pick, or whether the search is helping them.

Worth knowing: the written requirements for this version say under Non-Goals that there will be no logging of what people see or click in this release, and the story that would have built it was closed OBSOLETE. So this is almost certainly intended, and this check - which was written against the OLD search - is the thing that is now out of date rather than the product. Retiring it or rewording it is your call; I cannot change what a check expects on my own.

A report has been written up for this and is waiting on the QA lead's go-ahead before it is raised. [ticket_held]

title: Pressing Enter opens the top result without arrowing to it
comment:
Failed on staging (app.staging.shopview.com), workplace Staging Heavy Duty - 9919, build v26.39.1-02c6b6c, 28 September 2026.

Re-run on staging, where the suite now lives. Type a search, press Enter without touching the arrow keys, and you can open the wrong record - an unrelated company eight rows below the thing you searched for.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY HAPPENING - and it is not what I first wrote. The row sitting UNDER THE MOUSE POINTER becomes the one Enter will open. Clicking the search box leaves the pointer exactly where the panel then opens over it, so a row lands under the pointer and quietly takes over. Proved four ways on the same search:

  click the box and leave the mouse alone  -> the EIGHTH row is ready for Enter
  click the box, then move the mouse away  -> the FIRST row, correctly
  open with the keyboard, mouse in a corner -> the FIRST row, correctly
  open with the keyboard, mouse held over the middle of the list -> the row under it

This is the behaviour already reported and closed by the product team as no longer relevant. So the product is doing what was decided, and this check still describes the older behaviour.

I am recording it as Failed because the check, followed exactly as written, does not pass - but it needs YOUR decision on whether to retire or reword it, not a developer.

A report has been written up for this and is waiting on the QA lead's go-ahead before it is raised. [ticket_held]
